trent_sales: Quick POC question from Olga's team: they have SD-WAN -> TGW (multi-region active/active). Want PrivateLink into our connector in primary region and automatic fallback to an egress proxy in the secondary region. Requirement: preserve original client IP for logging and allow mutual-TLS. Also need an explicit minimal firewall port list and rough cost comparison to Hosted. Any gotchas?

nina_se: Short answer: doable. PrivateLink endpoints are regional, so you need a regional endpoint per region. For source IP preservation, use a TCP NLB fronting instances (targets as instances or IP mode with target preservation) and avoid NAT in the path. mTLS can terminate at the connector or be passed through depending on where certs are validated.

jasper_neteng: Clarifying Qs: 1) Does their SD-WAN announce prefixes to the TGW via BGP? 2) Will TLS be inspected at their edge or kept end-to-end? 3) Do they accept adding route automation to TGW route tables on failover?

olga_customer: We use BGP to the TGW. No TLS inspect - want end-to-end. We can do route automation if you provide a small runbook.

jasper_neteng: Recommended topology: deploy interface endpoint in primary region pointed at our NLB -> connector instances. In secondary region deploy an inbound egress proxy (another NLB + proxy fleet) and a separate endpoint. For failover use BGP local-pref change at their SD-WAN or an AWS route automation that swaps a prefix-list target in the TGW/route table. Note: cross-region failover will cause different egress path (and potential additional latency).

nina_se: Firewall minimal list to open on their side:
- Spoke/TGW -> endpoint ENIs: TCP 443 (API traffic)
- Endpoint health checks -> connector health port (TCP 8080 or configured port)
- If using mTLS: allow TCP 443 and exchange client certs/CA fingerprints
- Proxy (secondary) -> primary NLB for probes: TCP 443
We'll provide exact ENI prefixes and health-check IPs once we provision endpoints.

jasper_neteng: MTU/SD-WAN note: overlay tunnels can reduce PMTU; recommend MSS clamp on their edge. Also watch for asymmetric routing if they have hairpinning — that breaks source-IP expectations.

trent_sales: Cost notes (high-level): PrivateLink = hourly endpoint ENI + data processing per GB. NLB = hourly + LP data processing. Hosted has zero infra & per-token variable cost. Dedicated reserved capacity reduces variable per-token cost but requires monthly commitment and can reduce cross-region egress if we co-locate proxy. We'll draft a 1TB/month sketch.
